Ghusl is the full-body purification (washing) required in Islam for certain states of impurity (hadath akbar), such as after sexual intercourse (junub), menstruation (haid), or postpartum bleeding (nifas).
Ghusl becomes obligatory (wajib) after: janabah (sexual intercourse or emission), completion of menstruation (haid), completion of postpartum bleeding (nifas), and upon embracing Islam.
What is the difference between ghusl and wudu?
Wudu (ablution) is a partial purification washing specific body parts, while ghusl is a complete body purification that covers the entire body including rinsing the mouth and nose.
Can I pray without performing ghusl when it is required?
No. If ghusl is obligatory upon you (e.g., due to janabah, after haid, or nifas), you must perform ghusl before praying. Prayers without the required ghusl are not valid.
Is the niyyah (intention) required for ghusl?
Yes, the intention (niyyah) is a pillar (rukun) of ghusl. You must intend in your heart that you are performing ghusl to remove the state of major impurity (hadath akbar).
Are the answers from \"Ask the Scholar\" official fatwas?

No. The answers are AI-generated for general educational purposes about ghusl only. They are not official fatwas. For complex or personal cases, please consult a trusted local scholar or fatwa institution directly.
How do I use the \"Check Your Condition\" feature?

Tap \"Check Your Condition\" from the home screen or bottom navigation. Answer the Yes/No questions to receive general guidance on whether ghusl may be required for your situation. Remember: this is general guidance, not a fatwa.
